title: Chantilly Medicaid payments for durable medical equipment increase 10.7% in 2024
text:
Chantilly Medicaid payments for durable medical equipment increase 10.7% in 2024
L. F. Perez
Chantilly Medicaid providers billed $272,711 for services in the Durable Medical Equipment category in 2024, data from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database show. This represents a 10.7% increase over 2023, when claims for this category totaled $246,426.
Medicaid serves as a state-administered health insurance program that receives funding from both federal and state governments jointly. The program covers eligible low-income residents, seniors, children, and individuals with disabilities, making it one of the largest components of the U.S. health care system.
Since taxpayer dollars fund Medicaid, shifts in local billing amount reveal how public health care funding is allocated within the community.
The "Durable Medical Equipment" classification encompasses Medicaid-billed services based on standardized HCPCS and CPT code groups. This analysis assigned each billing code to a single service group by matching specific code prefixes and number ranges, enabling comparison of related services, preventing double counting, and maintaining consistent category rankings over time.
Overall Medicaid payments rose across several service groups, with Durable Medical Equipment ranking ninth by total Medicaid dollars paid in Chantilly in 2024.
On a statewide level in Virginia, Durable Medical Equipment placed 14th in overall Medicaid payouts during 2024.
Between 2019 and 2024, Medicaid payments for Durable Medical Equipment in Chantilly grew by $51,206, or 23.1%. Some years saw higher rates of growth, with notable increases occurring in 2020 and 2022.
Durable Medical Equipment spending occurred throughout Chantilly, though the majority of 2024 payments came from a small number of ZIP codes. The highest total for the year came from ZIP code 20151, accounting for $272,711. That single ZIP code represented 100% of Medicaid payments for Durable Medical Equipment in Chantilly during 2024.
Payments within the Durable Medical Equipment group were concentrated among only a few specific billing codes.
Comparing categories, the 10.7% jump in Medicaid payments for Durable Medical Equipment between 2024 and 2023 surpassed the 1.2% overall change observed across all Medicaid claim types in the city during the same period.
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services data show that combined federal and state spending on Medicaid reached approximately $871.7 billion in fiscal 2023—around 18% of the country’s total health outlays—climbing steeply from roughly $613.5 billion in 2019, before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
This jump equates to a growth of about 40% in just a few years, largely spurred by increased enrollment and greater use of Medicaid amid and following the pandemic.
Recent federal budget legislation during the Trump administration included major proposals to shrink federal Medicaid contributions and alter the program. The “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” enacted in 2025, is expected to cut more than $1 trillion from federal Medicaid spending across the next decade and brings new requirements for work and cost-sharing that may reduce funding and eligibility for some recipients. Such measures are set to shift additional costs to states and moderate the rate of federal Medicaid growth, though the program will continue to support tens of millions of Americans.
